title: Blank Line After Page Change Indicator

illustrates.quote: Insert a blank line after the page change indicator when the new print page starts with a format that normally is preceded by a blank line. (See Sample 1-2: Heading at Beginning of Print Page on page 1-22.)

blocks.features: Three vocabulary words ending the previous print page, one per line, no bullets or numbers.
Print page turn to page 360 ('#cfj': c=3,f=6,j=0), falling in the middle of the braille page.

blocks.text: Choose the letter of the answer that best completes each statement.
blocks.features: Instruction line opening the new print page, indented; normally preceded by a blank line (hence the blank line inserted after the page-change indicator, per 1.11.3.c, the rule this example illustrates).

items.text: Which of these is a bird of prey?

blocks.features: Numbered question with four lettered answer choices, a nested list.

pageBreaks.label: page change indicator, ending #cfj (new print page 360)

braille.notes: Ten lines, verbatim (an approx. 9-character page-layout margin measured and stripped; not real cell content). Line 5, immediately after the page-change indicator, is blank per rule 1.11.3.c because the new print page opens with an instruction/list format that would normally take a preceding blank line. The braille list of choices is truncated with '444' after choice 'b' in the source's own worked example.

resolution: Both runs agree on the mechanic (blank line after indicator, per 1.11.3.c) and on the vocabulary words/instruction/question wording; they differed on how to shape print.blocks (plain paragraphs vs. nested lists) -- resolved here using 'list' blocks for both the vocabulary words and the numbered question (matching the nested-list shape already proven in section-8's own buildListItem convention), since print itself shows these as a list, not running prose. Expected outcome: the braille excerpt truncates the answer list after choice 'b' with a '444' ellipsis (no print-side input to build the ellipsis itself from); built from the full print list (all four choices, per the print image), so Emboss's output is expected to run longer than the truncated braille -- a documented, expected mismatch, not a bug.
